report: Conclusion: **Supported, with qualifications.** In chronic HBV pregnancy with **high viral load/HBeAg positivity**, third-trimester tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) **as an adjunct to newborn vaccine plus HBIG** reduces mother-to-child transmission. The pivotal randomized trial enrolled HBeAg-positive mothers with HBV DNA >200,000 IU/mL; TDF from 30–32 weeks to 4 weeks postpartum cut transmission at 28 weeks from **18% to 5%** despite immunoprophylaxis (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/nejmoa1508660). A later Thai placebo-controlled trial starting at 28 weeks found very low transmission in both arms (**0% vs 2%**), so the difference was not significant—showing benefit is clearest when baseline risk is high (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1708131). WHO conditionally recommends TDF from 28 weeks until at least delivery for HBV DNA ≥5.3 log10 IU/mL, or HBeAg-positive if DNA testing is unavailable (https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/978-92-4-000270-8). A Lancet Infectious Diseases meta-analysis informing WHO found peripartum antivirals, especially TDF, highly effective without a major maternal/infant safety signal (https://www.thelancet.com/journals/laninf/article/PIIS1473-3099(20)30586-7/abstract). Thus: true for high-risk mothers, but not a replacement for timely birth-dose vaccine/HBIG.
